title: Berry-Curvature Effect in Anomalous Transport
abstract: A theory of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport in ferromagnets driven by statistical forces such as the gradient of temperature or chemical potential has been developed by Di Xiao et al in Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 026603 (2006) based on a field-dependent density of states generating an additional contribution to the current density. We present an alternative derivation of the Berry- phase effect in anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmertric metals based on quasiclassic matrix kinetic equation. Along with anomalous Hall effect an anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermalelectric currents are also derived.
summary: This paper develops a novel theoretical framework to calculate anomalous transport effects, such as anomalous heat and thermoelectric currents, in specific magnetic metals. It achieves this by adapting the quasi-classical matrix kinetic equation to the band structure. The work provides a robust derivation that reproduces known results while offering a distinct methodological approach.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide an alternative theoretical derivation of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport phenomena within altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals.
main_result: The derivation successfully yields expressions for anomalous heat flow, anomalous thermoelectrics currents, and confirms the anomalous Hall effect using the Berry curvature tensor.
method: The analysis employs the quasi-classical matrix kinetic equation, applied to the band representation of the electron distribution function.
model_or_system: The study models electron energy spectra in altermagnetic or noncentrosymmetric metals using a Hamiltonian structure involving Pauli matrices and a momentum-dependent pseudovector $\gamma(k)$.
key_observables: Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{ij}$), Anomalous Heat Current ($q_a^i$), Thermal Electric Current ($j_q^i$), and Thermal Electric Heat Flow ($q_E^i$).
important_parameters: The derivation is sensitive to the relative magnitude of the band splitting versus the scattering rate, and the presence of external fields (like magnetic fields).
main_assumptions: The core approximation used is that the band splitting strongly exceeds the scattering rate ($|\varepsilon_+ - \varepsilon_-| \ll 1/	au$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general quasi-classical matrix kinetic equation to the specific band representation, applies the necessary approximations, and then derives the anomalous contributions to current and heat flow, linking them to the Berry curvature tensor.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the use of kinetic equations and Berry curvature formalism connects to non-equilibrium dynamics, which has parallels in open quantum systems theory.
